subject: Cost floor and implementation handshake — Medisys pilot
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medisys.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, procurements@medisys.com
Cc: Marco Giordano <marco@vertexai.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing and migration feasibility for Medisys pilot

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we appreciated the walkthrough of runtime controls and the routing fallbacks. To move this forward with procurement we need a concrete comparison versus our incumbent (VertexAI) and a clear price-match proposal that addresses:

- A short pilot (6 weeks) with 100k tokens/day average and 500k bursts for 3 days/month
- A commitment to latency SLOs for 95th percentile under 250ms for 512-token requests
- Assurance on model parity (same open model family) and how fallback to quantized variants would impact accuracy

Attached is our RFP excerpt and cost sheet (Medisys_RFP_v2.pdf). We asked Marco (VertexAI) to share their standard pilot paperwork and he added context on their up-front credits.

Can you send a structured offer that aligns with our procurement timeline (decision by 06/30)? Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Elena
Procurement Lead | Medisys Health

--

Elena,

Appreciate the clear ask and the RFP excerpt. We can put together a short comparison and two concrete options for you by Friday. Quick clarifying questions to ensure the proposal is actionable:

1) For the pilot, is the burst pattern concentrated on specific dates (e.g., month-end analytics) or spread across teams?
2) Do you expect embedding workloads mixed with generation (rough split %)?
3) Any non-negotiable legal requirements (data residency or SOC-2 evidence beyond our standard pack)?

I'll loop in Jonas and Lauren to size the commercial offer and Connor to confirm runtime/latency enforcement and fallbacks. Attaching a working worksheet (redwood-match-options.xlsx) that we'll populate with scenario economics.

If you prefer a 30-minute sync, I can book something later today.

Best,

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Medisys — commercial framing and recommended playbook

Team,

Quick internal note after scanning the RFP: Medisys is price-sensitive but values predictable latency and an easy migration path. They called out VertexAI's up-front credits — that's our main anchor to beat. Two options I recommend we prepare:

Option A — Credit-forward match (short-term retention):
- 3 months of usage credits equal to ~60% of expected pilot spend (applied to hosted usage)
- 1 dedicated ramp day of capacity during their burst window (no extra charge for first month)
- SLA: 95th pctl latency target of 250ms for 512 tokens; automatic routing to dedicated pool when signal detects increased queueing
- Trade: no annual commit; product-level telemetry snapshot sharing in lieu of premium support

Option B — Reserved on-demand bridge (commit to retain):
- 6-month reserved capacity at a 20% discount to list with 1-month termination notice after 3 months
- Free egress for initial migration (to mitigate egress cost objections)
- Include an ops-runbook and a 2-week onboarding slot with Solutions (Connor lead) to validate model parity and microbenchmarks

Key open questions for Jasmine before we send:
- Which option best aligns with procurement (they asked for decision by 06/30 — a credit-forward option is faster to approve)
- Do we commit to a model-accuracy regression SLA or provide guardrails and a rollback policy to their incumbent?

I attached a quick ECR with numbers in the worksheet and a suggested one-pager to send. If we go credit-forward, we should present the economics as net-of-credit ARPU to avoid anchoring on large discounts.

-Jonas
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: redwood-match-options.xlsx (updated)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medisys.com>, procurements@medisys.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Cost floor and implementation handshake — Medisys pilot

Elena,

Thanks for the patience while we pulled a concise offer together — appreciate the quick turnaround window from procurement. Attached is a short offer doc and a one-page comparison (Medisys_Offer_v1.pdf) plus the worksheet we discussed. High level:

Summary of options

1) Pilot Credit Match (fast path) — recommended for procurement speed
- 3 months of usage credits equal to 60% of projected pilot spend (applies to hosted API tokens + embeddings)
- On-call ops during peak bursts for the first 30 days and one guaranteed capacity ramp day each month during pilot
- No upfront commitment; standard security pack + SOC 2 report provided
- Net economics framed as: effective 35% discount on pilot (credit applied to invoices)

2) Reserved Bridge (longer runway) — recommended if they want predictability
- 6-month reserved pool at 20% off list pricing; includes migration egress credit (first 10TB free)
- 2-week onboarding with Connor's team to validate model parity and microbenchmarks; rollback plan to incumbent if regression > 2% on agreed prompts

Operational notes
- Latency: Connor confirmed we can provision an autoscaled dedicated pool with 95th pctl ~240–260ms for 512 tokens under expected pilot load; we'll instrument traces and share a weekly latency report.
- Model parity: We'll run a 48-hour microbenchmark suite against their sample prompts and provide a report; fallback to a higher-precision variant is an option if accuracy dips.

Next steps
- If procurement wants the fastest approval, choose Option 1 and we will issue an official pilot addendum + DocuSign envelope by Monday.
- If they prefer the reserved bridge, we'll send a term sheet and a short SOW for the onboarding work.

Would you like us to schedule a 20-minute handoff with procurement and Connor on Monday to walk through the technical guardrails?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
